chapter: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
title: Lu joins the Baptist choir and quits
summary: Lu struggled with hymn timing in the Baptist choir, asked the Lord for a sign, and quit after not being called for her solo.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I'll tell you what happened. When I joined the Baptist Church, they kept bothering me to get in the choir. And I said, no, I didn't know no hymns, because I didn't want to get in the choir. So they kept on asking, so I said, "All right, I'll join the choir." So I joined the choir. Well, man, the Blues is different, because in these choirs, the meters are so long and the keys are lower. And then, I'm used to the music... When you play in the band, the band's going to make the harmony. Here it's with words! And I'd be looking all over the book for these words, and they'd say, "I don't see that in the book." That ain't in the book." So it took me about six months to get their timing, you know...

So I got mad. So I asked the Lord... I said, "Lord, I got mad with them..." And I said (??) to Danny. I said, "I ain't going back up in the choir because they argue(?) too much." So I asked the Lord, I said, "Well, Lord, if it's for me to be in this choir, keep me in. But if it's not, take me out." So the pastor, he came by and he said, "Mrs. Barker, I think you should go back in the choir." It's ...(?). So I said, "All right, I'm going to get back in the choir."

So I couldn't learn a hymn, you know, to do a solo. So I finally learned a hymn that I could do a solo. And I knew "The Whole World In His Hands" before I went back North(?). But I wanted to learn something else that I could do a solo. And I did. And this Sunday that I was going to sing this solo, they didn't call me. I had rehearsed it, and they didn't even call me. So I said, "Well, that's it." I said, "I ain't goin' back in that choir no more." So I didn't. They begged me, but I wouldn't go.
